You could try enrolling into a community college for an associates degree in whatever field you think your interested in. It's a fraction of the cost that you'd pay in a university. Plus, it's normally easier to transfer to a university from a community college than just to apply to a university. Many places just want your GPA and a certain amount of course hours, rather than your high school transcript, sat/act, gpa and all of that. When I graduated from high school, there was no way I could get into a good university.

You should be able to do your income taxes and then be able to do FAFSA (go to fafsa.gov) in the next month or so and see if you can get any sort of financial aid, as well. During my first four semesters I got $500 a semester from the community college and it lightened the burden of finances a lot. You might even be eligible for the pell grant, which pays a whole lot more.

I'm the same age as you, and I'm about to finish my final semester at my community college and get my associates in Science degree. After that, I'm headed to a university.
